concerns.text: SC‑002 requires a ≥10 % relative MAPE reduction versus a composition‑only baseline, but the plan provides no power analysis or sample‑size justification to ensure this effect is detectable with the expected test‑set size (potentially as low as ~150 materials). Without a statistical power calculation, the study may be under‑powered to reliably claim the improvement.

The plan mentions reporting bootstrap 95 % confidence intervals, yet it does not specify how many bootstrap resamples will be used, nor does it define a hypothesis‑testing procedure to confirm that the observed MAPE reduction is statistically significant rather than a random fluctuation.

Permutation importance and SHAP are both applied, but the plan only notes that “correlated descriptors are reported descriptively.” This does not adequately control for multicollinearity, which can inflate importance scores and lead to misleading conclusions about which structural features truly drive performance.

The baseline is a linear regression on Magpie compositional descriptors. Since composition is a subset of the structural information used by the GNN, the comparison may conflate the benefit of added structural features with model capacity. The plan lacks a control experiment (e.g., GNN trained on composition‑only features) to isolate the contribution of structural descriptors.
